answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the mirror hash is checked against the fable checkpoint at intake, the ripple audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. Scaling to 456 identities multiplies that fee by 823 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
